title: Needle instrumentation field notes — sampling pilot & dashboard parity
summary: Weekly capture from the ‘needle’ instrumentation experiment — notes from standups, quick wins, and unresolved questions. Focus areas: sampling heuristics, dashboard parity for latency-attribution, and a small cost telemetry uplift experiment.
content:
Purpose and context:
We kicked off the needle sampling pilot to validate a lightweight, rule-driven sampling strategy that targets outlier traces and high-cost routes while keeping ingestion down for lower-value requests. This doc is a running field notebook — not a final runbook. Use it to pick up context before the sync (03/15) and for handoffs if I'm OOO.

Standup highlights (2029-03-15):
- Arjun: baseline ingestion after enabling sampler v0.3 is ~1.8M spans/day (down from 3.9M) — initial CPU on the trace-processor fell ~22%. Saw a small uptick in tail latency attribution gaps for internal-inference route (p99 attribution missing for ~6% of sampled requests).
- Lena: dashboard parity work (migrating legacy span-lattice panels to new timeseries model) at 60% complete. Missing: per-route tokenized-latency panels and the correlating cost-by-token heatmap. Need a data model change request.
- Tom: ran cost telemetry uplift — introduced a cheap proxy metric (approx token-weighted CPU units) to approximate per-request cost. Proved correlation with billing at 0.86 Pearson for last 7 days.
- Priya: started A/B for sampling rules on dedicated customers — initial feedback: customer C sees more useful traces but complains about missing cold-start spans.

Recent experiments and results:
1) Rule-driven sampling (v0.3):
   - Rules: always-sample errors (HTTP 5xx), sample head-of-session for first N=3 requests, sample traces with CPU estimate > 50ms, and probabilistic floor 0.5%.
   - Outcome: ingestion dropped ~54%. Error surface coverage remains ~98% of error traces. Tail attribution drop concentrated on short-lived fast-path RPCs where KV cache hides execution spikes.
   - Next step: experiment hybrid rule where we increase head-of-session N to 5 for routes with > 95th token lengths in the last 24h.

2) Cost telemetry proxy:
   - Proxy formula: token_estimate * model_cpu_factor + fixed_overhead_per_req. Tuned factor using billing export.
   - Pros: cheap to compute at the gateway, good correlation with per-request billing.
   - Cons: underestimates when GPU batching yields nonlinear cost swings. Flagged a case where batch size changes produced a 1.7x error.

3) Dashboard parity migration:
   - Achieved parity for error-rate and latency-percentiles panels. Remaining: tokenized-latency breakdown (per-token contribution), and the cost-by-token heatmap. These require new derived fields in the traces->metrics transform.
   - Quick win: added a derived metric that approximates per-token latency by dividing total generation time by max(1, predicted_tokens). This recovers useful signal for 78% of traces.

Incidents & forensics:
- Incident 03/12: sudden flux in span-sampling rules caused a 30% disappearance of cold-start spans across staging. Root cause: a stale rule file in config-service (v1.2.4) that applied a higher probabilistic floor. Remediation: rollback and added CI linting for rule manifests.
- Follow-up: implement a canary config roll with a 5% traffic holdback and autoswitchback on coverage drop > 5%.

Action items (owner — due):
- (Arjun) Add a fallback that forces sampling of first-write spans of the KV cache path and test on staging (2029-03-22).
- (Lena) Draft data-model change request to include predicted_token_count and batch_size in trace->metric transformer (Jira: JIRA-OBS-7234) (2029-03-20).
- (Tom) Run a 48h validation comparing cost proxy against raw billing for different batch window sizes; capture divergence cases and thresholds (2029-03-25).
- (Priya) Run customer-facing study: enable heatmap for two Dedicated customers and collect feedback on debugging usefulness vs noise (2029-03-29).
- (Maya) Compose runbook snippet for sampler rollbacks including CI checks and playbook steps (2029-03-18).

Open questions & decision points:
- Sampling floor: Do we keep the global probabilistic floor at 0.5% or raise to 1% given new customer visibility needs? Tradeoff: +cost vs +debuggability for low-volume routes.
- Token granularity: should we store predicted_token_count in trace payloads (adds ~8 bytes/trace) vs compute heuristically in the transformer? Storage cost vs accuracy tradeoff.
- Cost-proxy failure modes: acceptable divergence threshold is currently undefined. What SLAs do we want for proxy correlation with true billing?

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a micro-backfilling job that fetches full spans for traces marked as "suspicious" by anomaly detector, rather than sampling them up-front. This could reduce steady-state ingestion while preserving forensics for flagged traces.
- Prototype a minimal client-side sampler flag that marks head-of-session with a short TTL — this would keep cost low and central config cleaner.
- Experiment: overlay batch_size heatmap with per-route concurrency; maybe we can schedule small batching windows for low-traffic routes to flatten cost spikes.

Quick logs from the lab (raw):
- 03/14 09:12 — ran sampler v0.3 against replay of 200k requests: error coverage 99.1%, ingestion 46% of original. CPU per-shard decreased from 58% to 44% median.
- 03/14 17:03 — tried tokenized-latency heuristic: for short traces (<10 tokens) heuristic breaks (noise). Marked these traces for exclusion in heatmap aggregation.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: missing cold-starting spans means some performance regressions will be invisible until customers complain. Mitigation: keep a low but nonzero cold-start head sample rate for every route and add customer-level opt-in for higher fidelity.
- Risk: dashboard parity changes might produce inconsistent numbers between old and new dashboards during migration. Mitigation: add a short-lived comparison view that surfaces differences and lists contributing traces.

Follow-ups for next sync (2029-03-22):
- Review JIRA-OBS-7234 (Lena) and approve data-model change if no major objections.
- Arjun to present staging test results for KV-cache-first-span fallback.
- Tom to show cost-proxy divergence heatmap and propose thresholds.
- Priya to share early customer study feedback.

Miscellaneous links and references:
- Replay bucket: gs://redwood-observability-replay/2029-03-14/needle-sample-run-1
- Dashboard (work-in-progress): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/needle/needle-sampler-v1
- Config manifest PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/config-service/pull/349

If you're skimming: key takeaways — sampler v0.3 saves ~50% ingestion, preserves error coverage, but loses some cold-start and short-fast-path attribution. We can fix most losses with small rule adjustments and a targeted fallback for KV-cache critical spans. Cost proxy is promising but needs divergence thresholds around dynamic batching.

Unresolved small TODOs (notes-to-self):

- schedule a 30-min runbook dry-run with SREs
- capture a short demo video for the customer study (Priya)
